pairs.subject: agent-cli-transport
pairs.evidence: src/stores/slices/agents/chatSlice.ts:277 Every turn that does not complete becomes the same generic 'something went wrong' error and Retry re-sends through startChatTurn, which resumes the same stored Claude session id (chat_turn::finish writes nothing on failure and has no 'thread gone' class), so a conversation whose Claude thread was pruned fails every retry and is never unbound, re-seeded or shown as a fresh thread.

techniques.evidence: src/stores/slices/agents/chatSlice.ts:280 The 'thread gone' and 'poisoned' verdicts are folded into a generic error. There is no typed 'thread lost' result, no unbind, and no shown re-thread (rules 1 and 4). Rule 3 is now partly met: the transcript lives server-side in the database (chat_turn.rs).

pairs.subject: agent-cli-transport
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/cli_args.rs:107 build_cli_args, and build_resume_cli_args at :329, emit --dangerously-skip-permissions unconditionally and expose no generate, readonly-scan or edit mode vocabulary, so no caller of this transport (including repo scans) can get a run that provably cannot write.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/cli_args.rs:329 The resume path also bypasses permissions. The optional --allowedTools (line 179) only pre-approves tools under bypass; it is not a restriction layer or a denylist.

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/cli_args.rs:110 The version requirement lives in a comment and the flag is hardcoded with no runtime version check or dated capability data, which is the baked-constant failure the technique names.
src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/cli_args.rs:103 '-p -' makes the prompt travel over stdin, never argv, as the contract requires.
